comments.text: Jump to the music initializer at $6C87. A selects an eight-byte song header at $7722; this load provides one header, song 0, and the ending calls this at $7C18 with A zero.
Jump to the per-update music driver at $6CEC. This copy updates all three SID voices, indices two, one and zero. The ending's text-scroll interrupt calls it at $86C7.
Jump into the initializer's three-byte fade-state reset. A is stored in $6C13-$6C15; the ending passes $0E here at $7C5F, once fire is pressed after the first text stage, to fade the song out.

Increment the music stop flag through $6DF2. While that flag remains set, later play calls write its value (one after a single stop) to all three SID control registers, which selects no waveform, and to the three fade-state bytes at $6C13-$6C15.
Current voice index, saved while helpers temporarily use X. The adjacent byte at $6C0D preserves an effect-record offset during pulse/filter modulation.
Effect-record offset preserved while Y indexes a pulse/filter sequence.

A nonzero value diverts playback to the stop branch, which writes this value (one after a single stop, so no waveform) to the three SID control registers and to the three fade-state bytes at $6C13-$6C15.
Primary tick countdown, reloaded from the song header's first speed byte.
Secondary tick countdown, reloaded from the second speed byte and controlling the primary tick cadence.
Primary tick reload copied from the selected song header and replaceable by order command $FB.
Secondary tick reload copied from the selected song header and replaceable by order command $FB.
Fade control value, tested by order commands and reset together with the two following fade-state bytes.
Fade countdown reload; when nonzero it enables periodic master-volume decrements.
Active fade countdown, reloaded from $6C14 until master volume reaches zero.
Filter mode bits OR-combined with the current volume when writing $D418.
Master volume, initialized to fifteen and decremented by the enabled fade path.
Three voice-indexed note-duration counters. The playback loop in this load processes voice indices two, one and zero.
Remaining duration for music voice index one, decremented together with the other two duration slots on the primary tick.
Remaining duration for music voice index two, decremented together with the other two duration slots on the primary tick. This load's playback loop emits all three voices.
Three note-duration values selected by pattern commands and copied to the active duration counters on notes.
Three update-age counters, reset on a new note and saturated at $FF.
Three byte offsets selecting eleven-byte instrument records at $7602.
Three instrument-selection addends installed by order commands.
Three sustain/release high-nibble overrides, initially zero and set by pattern commands.
Three offsets for the active instrument records, zero for the rest-duration command.
Three current note numbers, including the saved order-list transposition.
Three transposition addends installed by order-list commands.
Three byte positions in the selected note patterns.
Three byte positions in their order streams, including stream loop targets.
Three order-stream address low bytes copied from the song header.
Three order-stream high bytes, paired with $6C39.
Three remaining repetitions of the current pattern, installed by order-list commands.
Three waveform/control bytes, sent to the corresponding SID control register.
Three indices into command-driven waveform sequences.
Three indices into the instrument's related pitch sequences.

Three instrument behaviour flags, copied from byte 7 of the instrument record. Bit 1 lowers and bit 2 raises the frequency high byte by one each update; bits 0 and 3 select an age-derived pitch change; bit 4 suppresses the arpeggio; bit 5 zeroes sustain/release just before the note's duration runs out; bit 6 writes noise control $81 on the note's first update; bit 7 runs the waveform and pitch sequences and changes the gate timing.
Three nonzero arpeggio table selectors; zero disables the arpeggio helper.
Three positions within the arpeggio increment streams.
Three generated frequency low bytes sent to the SID voices.
Three generated frequency high bytes.
Three note-age thresholds before target-frequency slides start.
Three frequency-slide magnitudes. Reaching the target clears this field.
Three target note numbers for the frequency-slide helper.
Three byte positions in signed vibrato multiplier streams.
Three low bytes of the computed frequency difference used as the vibrato step.
Three corresponding high bytes for vibrato steps.
Three flags marking whether the current note's vibrato step has been calculated.
Three pulse-width low bytes followed by the shared filter cutoff low byte at $6C72. The modulation helper accepts X three for the filter.
Shared filter cutoff low byte, the fourth entry of the pulse/filter modulation-low array.
Three pulse-width high bytes followed by the shared filter cutoff high byte at $6C76.
Shared filter cutoff high byte, the fourth modulation-high entry.
Four pulse/filter direction states: zero rising, a positive value falling (four when loaded from bit two of the record's first byte, one after a reflection at the upper bound) and $FF stopped.
Four byte positions in the pulse/filter modulation streams.
Four remaining hold/repeat counts in the pulse/filter streams.

Three flags toggled by pattern command $FA. A set flag keeps a new note from reloading the pulse width and from resetting the pulse modulation's position, hold count and direction; the modulation itself keeps running.
Global filter-freeze flag toggled by pattern command $F9.

Multiply A by eight and read the selected song header. Set tick speeds, three order pointers and initial note durations; clear order/pattern positions, effect state and stop flags. Set volume fifteen and clear all three SID control registers. Fall through to the fade-state reset.
Store A into the three consecutive fade-state bytes and return. Initialization reaches here with A zero; the separate entry at $6C06 permits a caller-selected value.
Store A into the fade reload at $6C14 and active fade tick at $6C15, then return. Order commands enter here to change or clear the fade without replacing the separate parameter at $6C13.

If stopped, write the stop flag's value to all three SID controls and the three fade-state bytes, and return. Otherwise clear decimal mode, update fade and tick dividers, then process voices two, one and zero. Expired note durations parse order and pattern streams; other updates apply waveform, pitch, pulse and filter effects. Finish by writing the shared filter cutoff and mode/volume registers.

Save X as the active voice. If its duration is nonzero, update the current instrument effects. Otherwise clear per-note effect state, turn off the existing gate and parse its order stream at the saved position.

Interpret order bytes: $FF reads a byte-position loop target; $80-$BF set transposition; $C0-$DF set the instrument addend; $E0-$FA set pattern repeats. $FB replaces the tick speeds. While the fade parameter at $6C13 is zero, $FC clears the fade reload and tick and restores volume fifteen, and $FD stores its following byte as the fade reload and tick; with a nonzero parameter both leave the fade alone, and $FD still passes over its byte. $FE reaches the stop entry. A nonnegative byte selects a pattern through $776D/$777A.
Increment the stop flag and return. Subsequent play calls take the stop branch, which writes the flag's value to all three voice controls, selecting no waveform, and to the three fade-state bytes.

Select the pattern pointer and saved position. Commands set durations, release overrides, instrument/arpeggio selectors, filter/pulse freeze state or slide parameters. Notes below $60 apply order transposition; bytes $60-$7F select a rest duration. A following $FF ends/repeats the pattern and advances its order position when the repeat count expires.

Convert the selected note to frequency, load its instrument control, attack/decay and sustain/release, initialize pulse width unless frozen, and initialize shared filter parameters unless globally frozen. Write envelope registers and enter the normal SID control/output path.

Apply flagged direct high-frequency or age-derived pitch updates; a successful update skips the target-slide/vibrato branch. Otherwise run an eligible target slide or vibrato. Then process per-voice pulse modulation, shared filter modulation, arpeggio and waveform/pitch streams, in that order. Gate-timing flags can force early release or noise/reset control before output.
Select the voice's seven-register offset and write control, pulse width and frequency. Iterate to the next lower voice index, then write the shared filter cutoff and mode/volume.

Select waveform and pitch sequence pointers from the instrument's waveform mode. $FF reads a sequence loop position, $FE holds, and the pitch sequence's $FD advances then restores the base note frequency. Other pitch entries replace the frequency high byte and clear its low byte.
Operand byte 1 of the LDY instruction at $7139, in the ending's code. Instructions in this part that name it: sta at $7107 (write).
Follow the selected signed note-offset stream, holding on $80 and jumping to a byte index on $81. Add the current note number and look up its resulting frequency.
Use Y as a note-table index and copy low/high frequency bytes from $7402/$7462 into the active voice's frequency state.

Multiply the slide magnitude by four to form a sixteen-bit frequency step. Add or subtract toward the target note frequency; clamp when it crosses the target, then clear slide/vibrato state and make the target the current note.

On first use compute a frequency difference from an instrument-selected note offset and right-shift it by the selected scale. Later age bounds can adjust that step. Reset to the base note, read the signed multiplier stream and repeatedly add/subtract the step; $81 jumps to a stream index and zero holds the frequency.

Unless frozen for X, clear the modulation stream position and hold count and load its initial direction from bit two of the selected effect record. X zero through two select pulse width; X three selects the shared filter cutoff.

Read an optional modulation stream with loop, hold and repeat commands, or apply the record's constant steps: one word added while rising, another subtracted while falling. Compare against its upper/lower bounds; bit zero of the record's flag byte for that bound stops the modulation, bit one wraps to the opposite bound, and otherwise the direction reverses. Pulse-width and filter cutoff share this implementation through four state slots.

Four bytes of ASCII text, "SOS!", between the executable driver and its voice-register tables. No instruction reads them; the same letters open the signature text at $7757. They are why this driver's tables sit four bytes higher than the title's.
Fourth byte, "!", of the ASCII text "SOS!" at $73E1, before the voice-register offset table at $73E5. No instruction reads it.

Vibrato stream, ten bytes. The three vibrato records point at it (their pointers at $7693, $769B, $76A3), and update_music_vibrato reads it at $7283, one entry a pass: a positive entry adds the record's step to the frequency that many times (0, 1, 2, 1, 0), a negative one takes it away ($FF once, $FE twice, $FF once), and $81 is followed by the position to go back to, here $00. So the pitch rises and falls in a cycle of eight passes. The pulse and filter code reads its sixteen-byte records through bases from $76A3 to $76B2, with Y a nonzero multiple of sixteen, so instructions such as lda $76AA,y name addresses here without reading these bytes.

Three explicit high/low values ($0480, $03C0, $0310), then $FE, which hands over to the record's constant steps without advancing, so the hold and jump bytes after it ($90 $20, $88 $18, $84 $10, $FF $02) are not reached. Instruments 1 and 5 select record 1 for the filter and instrument 11 for its pulse width. The song header follows at $7722.

Run the ending's counter conversion, bitmap reveal, three-sprite movement, explosions, four-band sprite display and two-stage scrolling text. Each phase installs its own IRQ callback and waits on local state. Fade the ending song after fire, flush six blank text rows, close the bitmap window again, blank the display and return through the resident pointer at $0A40.

Bank normal I/O in, blank the display and clear the screen at $E000-$E3FF. Copy 1024 font bytes into $F000, enable all eight sprites and point the five leading ones at the solid shape $B7 in black, build a ten-row twenty-six-character counter panel and reset the local effects driver. Install ending-specific hardware IRQ/NMI vectors and a three-part raster chain, then enable the display.
Wait for the high raster portion through $D011, then select the blanked display-control value $6B.
Wait for raster line $C8, then run a 32-pass delay loop that outlasts that line, repeated input-X times: one pass a frame, so X frames.
Clear eighteen pages at $E400-$F5FF. Initialize the encrypted reader's descending key pointer to $8206 and its constants to $D3/$86; callers then set the encoded source pointer at $F600.
Save A/X/Y on the stack, acknowledge the VIC and jump through the local callback vector at $0003.
Restore Y/X/A from the stack and return from interrupt.

Select screen/character display settings and update five leading sprite Y positions. On a divided counter move the upper/lower reveal boundaries together or apart, then call the local effects driver and select the middle raster.
Set five sprite Y positions from the lower boundary and schedule the bottom callback at $DD.
Restore the top callback and selected VIC bank/character pointer, then convert one remaining-resource unit into score through $7ED0.

Process five categories: lives, continues, decimal timer units, diamonds and power lines. Each has a local rate and score addition. When a category reaches zero, pause and advance; after all five, mark conversion complete and start the boundary transition.
Indirect JMP through $9EB0 to $8A47, used by the scrolling-text parser.
Install three category-selected shape numbers, sprite positions/colours/expansion and a ten-character label. Then draw the selected remaining resource count without decrementing it.

On the selected category delay, test the resource, decrement it through its own BCD/decimal helper and request its score bonus. Zero ends this category and advances toward completion; the final category marks all conversion complete.

Operand byte 1 of the STA instruction at $7FF4, in the ending's code. No instruction in this part names it. The resident engine's jmp at $5447 names the address because it is the entry of the title file, which that code loads first.

Format seven BCD score digits into the resident panel's two rows and the ending screen's digit cells.
Decrement the resident lives byte in decimal mode, then format its two digits in the panel and ending screen.
Clear decimal mode and draw two digits of the resident life byte.

Mask the continue byte to its low nibble and draw one digit.
Decrement units with decimal borrow into tens/hundreds, reloading underflowed lower digits to nine. Continue into the three-digit renderer.
Draw the three separate decimal timer digits in panel and ending-screen cells.
Subtract one from the packed-BCD diamond byte in decimal mode, then draw its two digits.
Clear decimal mode and format both diamond nibbles into the panel and ending screen.
Subtract one from the packed-BCD power-line byte, then draw its two digits.
Clear decimal mode and format the two power-line nibbles into both displays.
Set the next raster from the second boundary and select bitmap display control before returning through the local IRQ exit.
Select the other bitmap/display-control phase and boundary callback. Move the two boundaries inward or outward according to the local completion flag.

Animate the three-part moving object through a sixty-four-entry trajectory and fifteen pose/duration entries. The first stage alternates an initial hold, then applies X/Y curves; the later stage accelerates X, adjusts Y on a divider and selects the corresponding three shapes. Finish by setting the local state negative.
Reset pose/state/dividers, initialize object origin and its first pose Y offset, then draw the three selected shapes and positions.
Select three shape numbers from the pose index and fall through to update their X/Y coordinates.
Derive two stacked sprite Y coordinates and a third adjacent X column from the object origin, pose offset and high-X state. Update the combined high-X bits.
Fifteen pose-selected vertical offsets for the three-part moving object.
Fifteen first-sprite pose shapes.
Fifteen second-sprite pose shapes; $FE selects the sprite slot at $FF80-$FFBF, which the ending's load does not supply.
Fifteen third-sprite pose shapes.
Fifteen pose duration values.
Fifteen pose-indexed step sizes for the departure: each is added to the object's X every frame and subtracted from its Y every second frame, so the steps of one, two and three speed it up.
Sixty-four signed X trajectory increments.
Sixty-four signed Y trajectory increments.
Update eight explosion sprite slots and the local effects driver, then return through the ending IRQ exit.

Each of eight slots has a delay and eight-frame shape index. On completion, set the slot's shape to $FE, the sprite slot at $FF80-$FFBF that the ending's load does not supply; while the global allocation count remains, reinitialize a new explosion at timer/program-byte-derived X/Y and request a selected sound channel.
Mix the CIA timer, an indexed instruction byte from $83B9, a constant and a second timer read, then invert the result. Input X selects the sampled program byte.
Four offsets selecting the resident request byte for the local effects driver.
Decrement the phase wait counter, set four sprite Y positions, call effects and select the first band callback.

Execute the fixed introductory loads and three NOPs as a delay, then select four shape numbers for the current band. Delay and place the next Y band until four bands are drawn; restore the starting callback afterward.

Copy four 256-byte source windows into $E400-$E7FF, the sprite shapes $90-$9F. The caller adds four to the high byte of each of the four source operands between repetitions, so each of the eight repetitions copies the next 1024 bytes, $9EB2 up to $BEB1 in all, producing successive picture phases.

Select text display control and service scroll state. Unless done or the keyboard pause input is active, decrement all nine row positions on a divided counter. Decode the next text row into a 192-byte glyph buffer and copy it into one of two interleaved sprite-row fields. Unless a completion marker was reached, decode and copy the second row with its own colour. Clear the foreground new-row flag afterward.

Clear the 192-byte glyph buffer.
